summary: High level sumary of our amazing project is the story is about NASA's Kepler Space Telescope, which was launched in 2009 to discover planets beyond our Solar System. Kepler used the transit method to detect planets by observing tiny changes in the brightness of stars. During its mission, it helped scientists discover more than 2,600 planets. In 2018, Kepler ran out of fuel and NASA retired it. Although its mission ended, its discoveries continue to help scientists explore and understand the universe.
details:
Our project is a creative storybook about NASA's Kepler Space Telescope, which was launched on 6 March 2009. It was designed to discover exoplanets, which are planets orbiting stars outside our Solar System. Kepler worked by observing the brightness of distant stars. When a planet passed in front of a star, the star's brightness became slightly dimmer. This method is called the transit method.

What benefits does it have?

  • Helps scientists discover planets beyond our Solar System.
  • Provides valuable information about distant planetary systems.
  • Helps scientists understand how planets form and develop.
  • Expands our knowledge about the possibility of other worlds beyond Earth.


What is the intended impact of the project?
The main purpose of this project is to educate and inspire people, especially students, to learn about space exploration and scientific discoveries. It encourages curiosity, creativity and interest in astronomy and technology.

What tools, coding languages, hardware or software did you use?
Our team used:

  • Hardware: Computer or laptop.
  • Software: Canva or other digital illustration and design software.
  • Tools: Internet research, digital drawing tools and storyboarding.
  • Coding languages: Not required because this project is a digital storybook rather than a programmed device.

    How is your project creative?
    Our project presents scientific information through an imaginative and interesting storybook. We personified the Kepler Space Telescope as a character with eyes and emotions, allowing it to tell its own story. We also used colourful illustrations, speech bubbles, captions and sound effects to make scientific information easier and more enjoyable to understand.

    What factors did your team consider?
    Our team considered:
  • Scientific accuracy: Ensuring all information about Kepler is correct.
  • Creativity: Making the storybook attractive and engaging.
  • Simplicity: Using easy-to-understand language.
  • Visual design: Choosing suitable colours, illustrations and layouts.
  • Educational value: Making sure readers learn something meaningful.
  • Teamwork: Dividing tasks and combining everyone's ideas.


    Project's Overall Impact
    Our project aims to show that science is not just about facts and complicated technology. It can also be shared through storytelling and creativity. Through Kepler's journey, readers can discover how one space telescope helped humanity explore thousands of planets beyond our Solar System.
